answers.reasoning: The distal wrist labels in the actual p16 raster are wrist bend, wrist yaw and wrist swivel. The revised citation now records all three. Competing sets mix in arm/base motion labels.

The circular arrow above the upright rear axis is labelled rotary motion. The side pivot is vertical motion and the along-arm linear arrow is radial motion; the new evidence text correctly separates these.

The vertical-motion label is beside the angular side-pivot arrow. This does not assert that every vertical motion is revolute; the question explicitly limits the reading to the schematic. The distractors swap identifiable arrow locations.

The actual platform figure labels top attachments as spherical joints, the telescoping leg as prismatic, and the fixed-base joints as U joints. The new citation supplies the raster labels omitted in v1.

The paired arrows run along the extensible leg, indicating extension/retraction. Long-axis rotation, perpendicular translation and whole-platform rotation are now distinct, plausible motion confusions rather than the old detachment distractor.

Following the PUMA serial chain outward gives waist, shoulder, forearm, then the three wrist rotations. The reverse order and the platform-joint list describe different directions or a different mechanism. The revised citation records the PUMA labels.

The revised stem asks for a correct distinction rather than a change that must occur. A stationary object can have a different coordinate description in another frame; position and orientation components depend on the chosen frame. The may-change answer is now logically compatible with the stem.

The slide contrasts some directly trajectory-executing actuators with the majority requiring force/torque computation. It explicitly says dynamics is central but not itself a complete solution. The revised alternatives test realistic inverse-kinematics, nominal-dynamics and command/effort confusions, while the stated scope avoids a universal stepper guarantee.
